title: Nearly 20 years after I first fell in love with In the Heights, this ...
transcript: In the Heights is one of my favorite musicals and New York City Center's gala production is consistently one of my theatre highlights of the year. This year, I made a very intentional decision. I was waiting until after the election to see it. I knew if things did not go well on Tuesday, I was going to need some joy. However, we know how Tuesday went. So this ended up being the perfect way to celebrate. The energy coming off that stage was just ridiculous. It felt like everyone was having the best night of their life. And this production of in the Heights is everything I've ever dreamed that a revival would look like. Matt Martinez is the perfect Usnavi had this delightful, charming, awkward charisma. Ismael Gonzalez as sunny brought me so, so, so much joy. And you've probably seen the viral video of Jackie Calderon telling Mandy Gonzalez that she's going to play Nina. That video made me cry. And then her performance in this made me weep. Breathe always hits in the Heights. It's such a profound impact on me and so many other people. And nearly 20 years later, it feels even more relevant. So much in this country is incredibly fraught right now. And a musical that celebrates immigrants and community and belonging and what it mean to find home, I can't think of anything more needed. And City Center launched an initiative to make 10,000 tickets under $28 with some as low as $5. And you could feel the difference in the audience. There were so many kids and first time theater goers and just enthusiasm in a way that I've not experienced in a long time. A powerful reminder that when we make the theater accessible, everyone benefits, not just the people seeing the show, but the artists on the stage and the entire community that gets to share in the experience. And then somehow the night got even better because I was invited to a talk back with the writers of in the Heights, Linmanuel Miranda and Kiera Algerra Huges. I was in trans. I literally could listen to them all night. And I left New York City center with the biggest smile on my face and a reminder why I love New York City so much. In the Heights is running at New York City Center through November 15, means this is a must see. And now the only question I have left is do we think this transfers to Broadway? I for one, really hope that it does.
